issues.title: Ranged enemies replace fatal death with an invulnerable dying-to-despawn path
issues.issue: Marksman and Sharpshooter intercept fatal damage, enter a 4.25-second immobile/invulnerable dying state, then instant-despawn while Attack's explicit NPC defeat settlement is owned by entityDie.
issues.observed: The ranged family uses fatal -> deals_damage:no -> start_dying -> movement 0 / damage disabled -> instant_despawn; CombatTracker increments npcKills and killedEntityConfigIds from entityDie.
issues.expected: Every defeated gameplay enemy has clear death feedback and exactly-once kill/score/retry-survivor settlement regardless of terminal presentation.
issues.resolution: Route every enemy terminal path through one explicit exactly-once defeat settlement owner; keep visual death presentation separate from authoritative settlement.
issues.technicalAnalysis: The selected artifact exposes an alternate terminal mechanism for ranged enemies without an explicit shared settlement owner. This also matches the tester-visible abrupt stop/disappearance symptom.

relevantCode.reason: CombatTracker defeat settlement is driven by entityDie.

mustPreserve: Kill bonus and retry survivor preservation

issues.title: Loading blackscreen can expose intermediate world frames
issues.issue: The transition intended to hide teleport/loading uses fire-and-forget camera/input commands, so acquire and release can overlap gameplay mutation.
issues.observed: beginLoadingVisual repeatedly fires camera fade and movement-lock commands without awaiting an opaque state; endLoadingVisual independently fires movement enable, camera clear and fade release.
issues.expected: Hidden loading is established before teleport/load and released only after destination readiness/final camera state.
issues.resolution: Use one ordered presentation owner: acquire/lock -> establish hidden state -> teleport/load -> readiness -> final camera -> release black -> release input.
issues.technicalAnalysis: There is no authoritative acquire -> mutation/readiness -> release sequencing boundary.

relevantCode.reason: beginLoadingVisual/endLoadingVisual own fade, camera clear and input release.

issues.title: Last-second flag capture can race timeout through competing terminal paths
issues.issue: FlagService delays victory one tick without a session/generation token; timeout can mutate timing/session state first.
issues.observed: scoreFlag schedules endGame(victory) one tick later; timeout can run first and clear the timestamp used by the later victory guard while scheduling retry.
issues.expected: Each attempt has exactly one terminal owner and later terminal callbacks cannot score/retry/advance it again.
issues.resolution: Claim terminal outcome atomically per arena/session generation and bind delayed victory to that claim/context.
issues.technicalAnalysis: Other delayed retry/advance work is context-guarded; the unguarded FlagService terminal callback is the specific remaining race.

issues.title: Level readiness is published while required enemy spawns can still be retrying or permanently missing
issues.issue: Level setup can start gameplay services and report ready while configured enemies have not materialized; retry exhaustion explicitly leaves the level active.
issues.observed: activateLevelInside starts FlagService/ContraptionService and returns with retrying > 0; retry exhaustion logs that the level remains active.
issues.expected: Required gameplay entities reach a terminal readiness disposition before the level becomes playable, unless a grounded degraded-mode design allows missing entities.
issues.resolution: Gate playable readiness on required enemy materialization/verification or select an explicit degraded-mode outcome.
issues.technicalAnalysis: Pending critical work is treated as readiness, allowing an incomplete configured combat population under spawn/chunk-loading failure.

relevantCode.reason: EntityLoader retry queue and activateLevelInside readiness/service start.

issues.title: Retry UI/title and chat communicate different retry information
issues.issue: Players receive different semantic payloads for the same retry decision.
issues.observed: Wipe/timeout title-subtitle surfaces expose different subsets while chat includes level, next attempt and score multiplier.
issues.expected: Retry surfaces derive from one authoritative information model for reason, attempt and multiplier.
issues.resolution: Build one retry presentation payload from authoritative attempt/tier state and project it consistently.
issues.technicalAnalysis: Scoring state itself is consistent; this is an information-projection defect.

issues.title: Lobby waiting-pad trigger is narrower than the visually communicated path
issues.issue: The visible waiting path is wider than the fixed join AABB, so visually valid edge positions can leave the admission trigger.
issues.observed: Each arena uses an approximately 7x7 join AABB; leaving it immediately invokes handleAreaLeave and can remove party membership.
issues.expected: Join trigger covers the intended visual waiting-pad footprint without overlap with neighboring pads.
issues.resolution: Align triggers to the authored visual pad/path footprint and verify neighboring triggers remain disjoint.
issues.technicalAnalysis: Source proves the trigger/leave behavior; the wider visual footprint is tester-observed evidence.

issues.title: Game-results export identifies v1.1.10 as v1.1.0
issues.issue: Machine-readable result provenance reports the wrong artifact version.
issues.expected: World/pack metadata and game-results export consume one canonical version and report 1.1.10.

issues.title: Ranged Archer-family presentation still contains melee/sword state machinery despite Bow-only design
issues.issue: Approved design is Bow-only at every distance, but ranged presentation/controller still authors swap_to_melee and melee states.
issues.observed: v1.1.10 spawns ranged enemies in ranged mode and no current writer to melee variant was proven, but obsolete melee/swap states remain authored.
issues.expected: Marksman/Sharpshooter remain ranged-only at all distances with no sword, melee attack or weapon-swap state.
issues.resolution: Remove melee/sword/swap state family for ranged enemies; keep Bow behavior at close range.
issues.technicalAnalysis: This is design cleanup, not proof that v1.1.10 currently reaches sword combat.

issues.title: Attack does not implement the approved crafting-UI disablement
issues.issue: Approved design requires crafting UI unavailable during Attack gameplay, but no crafting/inventory UI override or equivalent owner exists.
issues.observed: Selected BP/RP contains no crafting-screen/recipe-book UI override or gameplay owner disabling that surface.
issues.expected: Crafting UI is unavailable throughout Attack gameplay and no alternate crafting surface bypasses the restriction.
issues.resolution: Implement one explicit Attack crafting-availability owner and project it through UI/capability.
issues.technicalAnalysis: This is an approved design requirement not implemented in the selected artifact, not proof of a specific recipe exploit.

relevantCode.reason: No crafting UI override in selected RP.

issues.title: Team flag identity is absent during Waiting and appears only when gameplay services start
issues.issue: Approved design requires team flag visible during Waiting, but gameplay flags start with level activation.
issues.observed: FlagService.startForArena is tied to level activation; separate display_flag_pole_red/blue entities already exist.
issues.expected: Waiting shows a non-interactive team-identity flag; capture/objective behavior activates only in gameplay.
issues.resolution: Manage display-only flags during Waiting and transition to gameplay objective flags at ACTIVE.
issues.technicalAnalysis: Display ownership can remain separate from objective ownership, avoiding pre-start capture logic.

relevantCode.reason: Gameplay FlagService starts with level activation.

devNotes.title: Entity Selection Stick Is Still Active in Production
devNotes.problem: EntitySelectionLogger is initialized in the production Attack bootstrap. Any valid player using a normal minecraft:stick records coordinates and receives ctf_attack debug messages; sneaking with the stick removes/clears selections. The handler has no admin check.
devNotes.action: Remove EntitySelectionLogger from the release bootstrap, or gate the entire tool through the existing PermissionService admin owner. A normal gameplay item should not implicitly activate developer instrumentation.

evidence.finding: EntitySelectionLogger.init() subscribes to itemUse for minecraft:stick and is called unconditionally by the Attack bootstrap; addSelection() has no PermissionService check.

devNotes.title: World-Mutating Script Events Do Not Use the Existing Admin Permission Owner
devNotes.problem: Attack ships an explicit PermissionService, but GameManager script-event handlers for reset/force-start/force-end/skip-level and setup/reset services do not check PermissionService.isAdmin() before mutating session/world state. Command-level reachability may still restrict ordinary players, so this is not classified as an ordinary-player exploit from source alone.
devNotes.action: Route developer/admin script-event handlers through one explicit permission gate before performing world or session mutations. Do not rely only on external command reachability as the privilege boundary.

evidence.finding: GameManager receives ctf_attack reset/force/skip events and setup/reset services receive world-mutating script events without calling PermissionService.isAdmin().

devNotes.title: Admin Grant Secret Is Hard-Coded in the Shipped Behavior Script
devNotes.problem: permission.config embeds the admin grant/revoke secret directly in the distributed behavior script. Anyone with the world/add-on files can read the value, so it should not be treated as a durable secret boundary.
devNotes.action: Do not use a shipped static secret as the trust boundary. Prefer operator/host-controlled authorization or another runtime authority that is not recoverable from the distributed pack.

evidence.finding: permissionConfig contains a literal secretCode and PermissionService compares incoming set_admin/remove_admin messages against it.

devNotes.title: Attack Still Relies Heavily on Deprecated Async Command Calls
devNotes.problem: The v1.1.2 compiled behavior scripts contain 34 runCommandAsync() call sites. This is technical-debt/API-migration risk rather than a proven current gameplay failure.
devNotes.action: Migrate command-backed operations to supported direct APIs or the current command surface where practical, prioritizing lifecycle-critical inventory, ticking-area, setup, camera, and reset paths. Keep behavior parity while migrating.

evidence.finding: Full compiled-script scan counts 34 occurrences of runCommandAsync(): 22 in chunk-4L7PEIZ4.js, 6 in chunk-EJPDS27P.js, and 6 in chunk-UUF652QC.js.

devNotes.title: Dedicated Shop-Item Preservation Helpers Are Dead Code
devNotes.problem: KitManager defines capturePersistentShopItemsFromManagedSlots() and restorePreservedShopItems(), and startBuyPhase carries a preservePersistentShopItems option, but the current production loadout path does not call those helpers. Actual survival of purchases relies on generic non-kit item displacement/preservation behavior instead.
devNotes.action: Remove the unused preservation path or connect one clear inventory-preservation owner. Avoid maintaining a named preservePersistentShopItems contract that is not actually consumed by applyPlayerLoadout().

evidence.finding: Full production-script search finds definitions of capturePersistentShopItemsFromManagedSlots()/restorePreservedShopItems() but no callers; applyPlayerLoadout() ignores preservePersistentShopItems and preserves non-kit items through clearKitManagedItems plus slot displacement.

devNotes.title: Kit selection can immediately refresh loadout without an explicit gameplay-phase gate
devNotes.problem: setSelectedKit() persists the selection, clears effects and immediately calls applySelectedKitNow(). The registered loadout eligibility checker only enforces fresh-inventory readiness, not buy_phase versus active gameplay.
devNotes.action: If kit changes are preparation-only, gate the effect commit through the authoritative arena session phase. Keep UI visibility separate from authorization.

evidence.finding: Kit selection immediately reaches applyPlayerLoadout(); GameManager registers only isFreshInventoryReady() as the loadout eligibility checker.
